records.title: Production image now ships AnA's Python DOCX runtime: workers copied, pinned python-docx/lxml virtualenv, import probe, and CI builds the image
records.evidenceAtHead: Dockerfile.optimized:89-95 creates /opt/docx-runtime venv, pip-installs python-docx and lxml at the requirements.txt:19-20 pins (python-docx==1.2.0, lxml==6.1.1), runs a build-time `import docx, lxml.etree` probe (image fails to build otherwise) and sets ENV ANA_DOCX_PYTHON; Dockerfile.optimized:172 `COPY --from=builder /app/workers/artifact-compute ./workers/artifact-compute` (at 92ccdba1 the file had 0 references to workers/). server/services/compute/scriptWorker.ts:52,65 and workerClient.ts:20,51 resolve the runtime from cwd (/app) and spawn `process.env.ANA_DOCX_PYTHON || 'python3'`. workers/artifact-compute holds the 4 runtimes (docx-insert/xml/validate/python). `node scripts/ci/check-image-document-runtime.mjs` at HEAD -> `OK — 4 runtime(s) copied, their imports installed and probed.` Its self-test scripts/ci/__tests__/image-document-runtime.test.mjs (failing-first cases removing the COPY and the venv) runs in CI via `npm run test:ci-scripts` (ci.yml:1127). ci.yml:2100-2121 job production-image-boot builds `--target production` on every CI run; GitHub run 38358525641 (commit 9a59bc8f9, ancestor of HEAD, zero diff since in Dockerfile.optimized/requirements.txt/workers/server/services/compute) shows step 'Build the provision and production images' = success. .dockerignore excludes neither workers/ nor *.py. Caveat (tracked elsewhere, OPS-02/D1): the same CI job is red at its later 'Provision the empty database' step, so the image is built but not yet boot-proven end to end.
records.fixedBy: 2eda0ed0f (Dockerfile.optimized:79-95,171-172; scriptWorker.ts:65; workerClient.ts:51; scripts/ci/check-image-document-runtime.mjs + __tests__/image-document-runtime.test.mjs); a3df3cb0c (ci.yml production-image-boot builds Dockerfile.optimized --target production in CI)
records.severityRationale: The production image copies every runtime the server spawns, installs the pinned python-docx/lxml into a dedicated venv, refuses to build if they cannot import, and points both spawners at that interpreter; CI builds that exact target on every push, so the production-only failure mode is closed.
records.humanTestingNote: Only relevant to testers running from a source checkout instead of the Docker image: the spawners fall back to system `python3`, so AnA DOCX insert / surgical XML edit / validate_docx tool calls fail unless `pip install -r requirements.txt` (python-docx 1.2.0, lxml 6.1.1) was run or ANA_DOCX_PYTHON points at an interpreter that has them. In the Docker image this is handled.

records.title: Deploy now requires a green CI verdict for the SHA and pins/scans the digest, but there is still no staging stage, production rebuilds instead of promoting, and nothing rolls back automatically
records.evidenceAtHead: Closed part: .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:94-145 job ci-verdict reads the newest push run on concept2cure-v2 of ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml for the exact SHA and refuses anything but success (pinned by tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts); build-push needs it (:258-260); Trivy image scan blocks the ECR push on HIGH/CRITICAL (:329-341); deploy-api registers a task def pinned to <repo>@sha256:<digest> (:835-905); deploy-frontend runs only after deploy-api succeeds (:948-966); CI's production-image-boot builds the same Dockerfile target at the same SHA (ci.yml:2114-2121). None of this existed at 92ccdba1 (`git show 92ccdba1:.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml | grep -c ci-verdict` -> 0). Still open: the workflow is named 'Deploy to AWS (Production)' and the env block hard-codes production names (:29-81: AWS_REGION us-east-1, ECR_API_REPO c2c-prod-api, ECS_CLUSTER c2c-production, FRONTEND_BUCKET c2c-prod-frontend); `environment: production` is literal at :399, :821, :959; triggers are only `v*` tags and dispatch (:17-19); build-push rebuilds from source (`docker build -f Dockerfile.optimized --target production` :319-327) and deploy-frontend re-runs `npm ci && npm run build` (:967-974) instead of promoting the CI-tested artifact; terraform/environments/staging is targeted only by terraform-compliance.yml, which is pull_request-only and runs `terraform validate`; cerv2-staging-deploy.yml targets docker-compose/Vercel, not AWS; smoke-test (:1016-1072) has no rollback job (rollback is a manual `aws ecs update-service` per comments at :845-850). Recent CI runs on concept2cure-v2 (e.g. 38358525641, 38355530765) conclude failure, so ci-verdict would refuse every deploy today (OPS-02).
records.fixedBy: 8060c28bc (deploy-aws.yml ci-verdict gate + Trivy image scan before push); efdb0fb7b (frontend publishes after the API); a3df3cb0c (CI builds and boots the production image target)
records.remaining: 1) No AWS staging stage: deploy-aws.yml is production-only and no workflow applies or deploys terraform/environments/staging. 2) The production deploy rebuilds the image and the frontend from source rather than promoting the digest/bundle CI or staging tested (Debian apt packages in Dockerfile.optimized:64-77 are unpinned, so two builds of one SHA can differ). 3) No automated rollback when the post-deploy smoke test fails. 4) Dead cerv2-staging-deploy.yml is a parallel 'staging' path that deploys nothing to AWS.
records.severityRationale: The pilot target is a single AWS production environment, and the most dangerous half of the original finding (any tag deploys an unproven SHA) is closed by the ci-verdict gate plus CI building and boot-testing the same Dockerfile target at that SHA. What remains (staging rehearsal of migrations/terraform against a populated database, build-once-promote, automated rollback) is CSV/GxP release-discipline work expected before enterprise GA, not a blocker for a founder-supported pilot.
records.humanTestingNote: Not observable as a defect in the apps. Context for the test plan: the pipeline provides no AWS staging, so human testing runs on a local or docker-compose stack, which does not exercise CloudFront routing, the S3 vault, the KMS signer or the ECS task definition; AWS-only defects will not surface in this round.
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), merge never rebase.
1. Founder: decide staging topology (separate AWS account recommended, or same account with distinct stack names) and region; record it where terraform/environments/staging/main.tf backend and tfvars can use it. Apply terraform/environments/staging once (depends on OPS-01/03/04).
2. In .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml add a first job `resolve` that outputs `target`: `staging` for `rc-*` tags, `production` for `v*` tags, and a new workflow_dispatch choice input `target` (staging|production). Add `rc-*` to the push.tags list at :17-19. Rename the workflow 'Deploy to AWS'.
3. Create GitHub environments `staging` and `production`, each with vars AWS_REGION, ECR_API_REPO, ECS_CLUSTER, ECS_API_SERVICE, ECS_API_TASK_FAMILY, ECS_MIGRATE_TASK_FAMILY, FRONTEND_BUCKET and secrets AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, AWS_BUILD_ROLE_ARN, CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID; give `production` required reviewers. Delete the hard-coded values in the workflow-level env block (:29-81) and read them from `vars.*`/`secrets.*` at job level; replace the literal `environment: production` at :399, :821, :959 (and add it to build-push and smoke-test) with `environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.target }}`.
4. Build once: make build-push (:258-385) run only when target=staging. Keep its Trivy scan and digest capture; tag the image `sha-${GITHUB_SHA::12}` (ECR tags are immutable). The frontend is already inside the image (production stage copies /app/dist, which contains dist/public), so deploy-frontend must stop rebuilding: replace :967-974 (`npm ci`, `npm run build`) with `docker pull <repo>@<digest>`, `docker create`, `docker cp <id>:/app/dist/public ./dist/public`.
5. On staging smoke-test success (:1016-1072) add a step that writes an additional ECR tag `staging-verified-${GITHUB_SHA::12}` onto the same manifest (`aws ecr batch-get-image` then `aws ecr put-image --image-tag ... --image-manifest ...`).
6. Production path (target=production): add a `promote` job that does NOT run docker build. It looks up `staging-verified-${GITHUB_SHA::12}` with `aws ecr describe-images`, refuses (exit 1, fail closed) when absent, and outputs its imageDigest; wire migrate, deploy-api (IMAGE_DIGEST at :839-840) and deploy-frontend to that output instead of build-push. If staging and production are separate accounts, add ECR cross-account pull or registry replication in terraform/modules/ecr and grant the production deploy role ecr:BatchGetImage on the staging repo.
7. Rollback: in deploy-api, before update-service (:907-916), capture `aws ecs describe-services --cluster $ECS_CLUSTER --services $ECS_API_SERVICE --query 'services[0].taskDefinition' --output text` as output `previous_td_arn`. Add job `rollback` with `needs: [deploy-api, smoke-test]`, `if: always() && needs.deploy-api.result == 'success' && needs.smoke-test.result == 'failure'`, that runs `aws ecs update-service --task-definition <previous_td_arn>` and `aws ecs wait services-stable`. Comment that this is safe because migrations in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES are additive (Rule 1); a non-additive migration requires a manual decision.
8. Delete .github/workflows/cerv2-staging-deploy.yml in the same change (zero duplication); the commit message names deploy-aws.yml's staging target as its replacement and the contract test in step 9 as the reachability proof. It is a workflow, not a user-facing capability.
9. Extend tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts with assertions that (a) no job reachable when target=production contains `docker build` or `npm run build`; (b) production resolves its digest only via `staging-verified-`; (c) a rollback job exists conditioned on smoke-test failure; (d) no literal `environment: production` remains. Run it against HEAD's deploy-aws.yml first and keep the failing output, then make it pass.
records.acceptance: 1) Failing first: the new assertions in tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts fail on HEAD's deploy-aws.yml (docker build at :319-327, npm run build at :973-974, no rollback job, literal environment: production) and pass after the change. 2) An `rc-*` tag deploys to staging, the staging smoke test reports /readyz ready through the staging CloudFront alias, and ECR shows `staging-verified-<sha12>` on the built digest. 3) A `v*` tag on the same SHA runs no build step, and `aws ecs describe-task-definition` shows the production API container image digest equal to the staging one. 4) A `v*` tag on a SHA without `staging-verified-` is refused before migrate. 5) Forcing the staging smoke test to fail (e.g. a dispatch with a deliberately broken readiness URL) triggers the rollback job and the service returns to the previous task-definition revision.
records.dependencies: OPS-01 (first apply/deploy), OPS-02 (CI must be green or ci-verdict refuses every deploy), OPS-03 (state bucket names), OPS-04 (RDS version), founder decision on staging AWS account/topology and budget.

records.title: Launch config in IaC: MCP connector, Anthropic key and the PDF/A rule are now settled; SENTRY_DSN is optional and there is still no REDIS_URL (rate limits are per replica)
records.evidenceAtHead: Closed: terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277 sets MCP_ENABLED=true, MCP_PUBLIC_URL=local.app_origin, MCP_CLIENT_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST in boot_environment (absent at 92ccdba1); server/index.ts:120 still mounts only on 'true'; .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514-522 preflight requires MCP_ENABLED, MCP_PUBLIC_URL, MCP_CLIENT_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and :695-705 checks MCP values (exactly 'true', https origin, non-empty allowlist). ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is a required boot secret (main.tf:326; terraform/stack/variables.tf:351-356 validates sk-ant-); OpenAI is opt-in per Order Form (variables.tf:328-340). ECTD_REQUIRE_PDFA: server/services/ectd/pdfa-requirement.ts:1-20 makes PDF/A required only when the deployment or the organisation opts in; the per-org setting settings.submission.requirePdfA has a UI (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/PdfARequirementSetting.tsx) and is enforced before transmit (server/services/submission-gateways/index.ts:230, resolvePdfARequirement throws when the setting cannot be read). FDA accepts plain PDF 1.4-1.7, so the absent env flag is now a deliberate rule, not a gap. Still open: SENTRY_DSN defaults to "" (terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:181-184), observability_environment is empty when unset (main.tf:338) and SENTRY_DSN is not in the preflight list (deploy-aws.yml:514-522). REDIS_URL: `grep -rni redis terraform/` -> nothing; server/startup/env.ts:104-110 only warns; server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:96-101 falls back to a per-process Map, with api_desired_count=2 (environments/production/variables.tf:48-51), so auth and documents limits are per task and reset on every deploy.
records.fixedBy: 42842480f (MCP_* in terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277 + deploy preflight); c3e9e4930 (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY boot secret); 19d2be04a (Sentry configurable, OpenAI key validated); 4fdafc362 (PDF/A rule: pdfa-requirement.ts, per-org setting, transmit guard)
records.remaining: 1) SENTRY_DSN can be omitted: no validation requires it and the deploy preflight does not check it, so production can ship with no error reporting (overlaps OPS-06). 2) No Redis or other shared store in terraform/: REDIS_URL is never set, so rate limiting (including the fail-closed auth and documents buckets) is per process across the 2 API tasks and resets on each deploy; boot only warns.
records.severityRationale: The items that turned launch features off silently are closed: the remote MCP connector is mounted and preflight-enforced, a drafting-approved Anthropic key is required, and PDF/A is now an explicit per-org/per-deployment rule. The residual is observability (already carried as OPS-06 at P1) and per-replica rate limiting, which doubles brute-force thresholds on a login that still requires the mandatory email OTP. That is hardening before enterprise GA, not a pilot blocker.
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. Founder decisions, recorded before code: (a) Sentry as a subprocessor (DPA, data region, PII scrubbing) or CloudWatch-only error reporting under OPS-06; (b) shared rate-limit store: ElastiCache (Redis/Valkey) is recommended. A Postgres table keyed by IP/email would conflict with CLAUDE.md Rule 1's `organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL` requirement for pre-authentication keys.
2. If ElastiCache: add terraform/modules/elasticache-redis/ with aws_elasticache_subnet_group (module.vpc.private_subnet_ids), a security group admitting 6379 only from module.ecs.ecs_tasks_security_group_id, and aws_elasticache_replication_group with transit_encryption_enabled=true, at_rest_encryption_enabled=true, kms_key_id, auth_token from random_password, automatic_failover_enabled=true, multi_az_enabled=true, num_cache_clusters=2. Instantiate it in terraform/stack/main.tf.
3. Add a `redis_url` entry to module "secrets" (terraform/stack/main.tf:116 onward) with value `rediss://:<auth_token>@<primary_endpoint_address>:6379`, and add `{ name = "REDIS_URL", value_from = module.secrets.secret_arns["redis_url"] }` to local.boot_secrets (main.tf:316-331).
4. Sentry (if chosen): change terraform/stack/variables.tf:424-430 validation to require a non-empty https DSN, remove the "" default in terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:181-184 and the staging equivalent, document it in terraform.tfvars.example, and confirm server/utils/sentry.ts scrubs request bodies and user identifiers before send. If CloudWatch-only is chosen instead, remove 'SENTRY_DSN' from the recommended list in server/startup/env.ts:105 and record the decision under OPS-06.
5. Add REDIS_URL (and SENTRY_DSN if chosen) to the preflight loop in .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514-522 and extend the ::error:: text at :541.
6. Fail closed at boot: in server/startup/env.ts:104-110, when NODE_ENV=production and neither REDIS_URL nor REDIS_TLS_URL is set, refuse to start unless RATE_LIMIT_ACCEPT_MEMORY=true (same pattern as STORAGE_ACCEPT_LOCAL_DISK). Add RATE_LIMIT_ACCEPT_MEMORY=true to the CI single-container boot envs (ci.yml production-boot-smoke env and the production-image-boot app.env heredoc around ci.yml:2163-2190) so those jobs keep booting.
7. Tests, each shown failing on HEAD first: (a) a terraform test in terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl asserting REDIS_URL is in the API container secrets (and SENTRY_DSN in its environment if chosen); (b) a contract test under tests/ci/ asserting the deploy preflight list contains REDIS_URL; (c) a unit test that production boot without REDIS_URL and without RATE_LIMIT_ACCEPT_MEMORY exits non-zero; (d) a rate-limiter test with two limiter instances sharing one Redis (ioredis-mock or a container) showing the auth bucket counts across both.
records.acceptance: 1) Failing first: the new terraform test, the preflight contract test and the boot-refusal test all fail against HEAD and pass after the change. 2) `terraform test` in terraform/stack passes in terraform-tests.yml. 3) The deploy preflight refuses a task definition without REDIS_URL (and without SENTRY_DSN if Sentry is chosen). 4) On a deployment with 2 API tasks, failed sign-in attempts against one account spread across both tasks are refused at the configured auth limit (not twice that), and the count survives a rolling deploy. 5) If Sentry is chosen, a deliberately thrown test error in staging appears in Sentry with no request body or email in the event.
records.dependencies: OPS-06 (monitoring/Sentry), OPS-13 / OPS-20 (Redis decision and scaling), OPS-01 (first apply), founder decisions on Sentry DPA and Redis budget.

records.title: VPC: S3 and KMS endpoints now carry traffic, but there is still one NAT gateway in AZ-a and no ECR/Secrets Manager/Logs/STS endpoints
records.evidenceAtHead: Closed: terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:92-98 S3 gateway endpoint now has `route_table_ids = [aws_route_table.private.id]` (at 92ccdba1 it had none); :102-110 KMS interface endpoint has `private_dns_enabled = true` in every private subnet; :112-130 endpoint SG admits tcp/443 from the VPC CIDR only (at 92ccdba1 it had no ingress). terraform/modules/vpc-secure/tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl asserts each of these and runs in .github/workflows/terraform-tests.yml (matrix entry terraform/modules/vpc-secure, :55). Still open: one aws_eip.nat and one aws_nat_gateway.this in aws_subnet.public[0] (:57-67); a single aws_route_table.private routes 0.0.0.0/0 to that NAT for all private subnets (:69-82); no aws_vpc_endpoint for ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, logs or sts anywhere in terraform/modules/vpc-secure; terraform/modules/vpc-secure/variables.tf has no per-AZ NAT option. ECS task SG egress is 0.0.0.0/0 through the NAT (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:117-125).
records.remaining: Single NAT gateway in AZ-a carrying all private egress for both AZs: losing AZ-a (or that NAT) stops ECR API calls (new tasks cannot pull), Secrets Manager fetches (new tasks cannot start), CloudWatch Logs delivery, SMTP (login OTP, so no one can sign in) and AI-provider calls in both AZs. ECR/Secrets Manager/Logs/STS traffic also pays NAT data-processing charges.
records.severityRationale: What remains is availability during a rare AZ-level failure plus NAT cost. It is not security, tenant-isolation or data-integrity exposure, and a founder-supported single-customer pilot can accept an AZ-outage window. The billed-but-dead endpoints and NAT-routed Vault/KMS traffic are fixed. Per-AZ egress belongs before enterprise GA and any availability SLA.
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. In terraform/modules/vpc-secure/variables.tf add `variable "nat_gateway_per_az" { type = bool, default = true }` and `variable "interface_endpoints" { type = list(string), default = ["kms", "ecr.api", "ecr.dkr", "secretsmanager", "logs", "sts"] }`.
2. In terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:57-67 give aws_eip.nat and aws_nat_gateway.this `count = var.nat_gateway_per_az ? length(var.public_subnets) : 1`, with subnet_id = aws_subnet.public[count.index].id and per-index Name tags.
3. Replace the single aws_route_table.private (:69-76) with `count = length(var.private_subnets)`, each routing 0.0.0.0/0 to `aws_nat_gateway.this[var.nat_gateway_per_az ? count.index : 0].id`, and point aws_route_table_association.private (:78-82) at aws_route_table.private[count.index].id. This assumes private_subnets[i] and public_subnets[i] share azs[i], which the module already does via element(var.azs, count.index); add a validation that the two lists have equal length.
4. Add `moved` blocks (aws_eip.nat -> aws_eip.nat[0], aws_nat_gateway.this -> aws_nat_gateway.this[0], aws_route_table.private -> aws_route_table.private[0]) so a plan against any existing state does not destroy and recreate the egress path.
5. Change the S3 gateway endpoint (:96) to `route_table_ids = aws_route_table.private[*].id`.
6. Replace the single aws_vpc_endpoint.kms (:102-110) with `resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "interface" { for_each = toset(var.interface_endpoints) ... service_name = "com.amazonaws.${var.region}.${each.key}", vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface", subnet_ids = aws_subnet.private[*].id, security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.endpoint.id], private_dns_enabled = true }` plus `moved { from = aws_vpc_endpoint.kms  to = aws_vpc_endpoint.interface["kms"] }`. Update the KMS assertions in tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl to the new address.
7. Expose nat_gateway_per_az in terraform/stack/variables.tf and pass it into module "vpc" at terraform/stack/main.tf:15-24; set true in terraform/environments/production and allow staging to set false for cost.
8. Extend terraform/modules/vpc-secure/tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl, running it against HEAD's main.tf first and keeping the failing output: length(aws_nat_gateway.this) == length(var.public_subnets); each aws_route_table.private[i] routes to the NAT whose subnet is public[i]; the S3 endpoint is associated with every private route table; aws_vpc_endpoint.interface contains ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, logs and sts with private_dns_enabled = true. terraform-tests.yml already runs this module.
records.acceptance: 1) Failing first: the new assertions fail on HEAD's terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf (one NAT, one private route table, no ECR/Secrets Manager/Logs/STS endpoints) and pass after the change; terraform-tests.yml is green for terraform/modules/vpc-secure and terraform/stack. 2) After apply: `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways` shows one available NAT per AZ; each private subnet's route table targets the NAT in its own AZ; `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints` lists s3 (gateway, on every private route table) and kms, ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, logs, sts (interface, PrivateDnsEnabled=true). 3) Staging failure drill: with the AZ-a NAT route removed, a new API task launched in AZ-b pulls its image, fetches its secrets, writes logs and sends a login OTP.
records.dependencies: OPS-01 / OPS-03 (first terraform apply), founder budget approval (one extra NAT gateway plus about six interface endpoints per AZ, billed hourly).
